# Monocurl Essays

> Free visual lessons in algebra, geometry, trigonometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, physics and more. Every idea is drawn and animated, and every figure's source is open.

Each lesson is self-contained and free to read. A plain markdown copy of every lesson is at the lesson URL followed by `index.md`. Figures are animations written in the Monocurl language (https://www.monocurl.com); the markdown copies describe each figure by its caption.

## Algebra

Visual algebra lessons: negative numbers, the distributive law, completing the square, the quadratic formula, slope, systems of equations and exponents, each one drawn and animated.

- [Why is a negative times a negative positive?](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/algebra/negative-times-negative/index.md): Multiplying by a negative number flips the number line about zero, and two flips cancel. We see it, then prove it from the distributive law.
- [The distributive law as a picture: FOIL and (a+b)²](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/algebra/distributive-law-area/index.md): Cutting a rectangle into pieces explains FOIL, why (a+b)² has a middle term 2ab, and why (a+b)(a−b) = a² − b². Each identity is then proved.
- [Completing the square and the quadratic formula](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/algebra/completing-the-square/index.md): Solve x² + 6x = 16 by rearranging a square and a rectangle into a bigger square with one corner missing, then turn that picture into the quadratic formula.
- [What slope means, and why y = mx + b is a line](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/algebra/slope-and-lines/index.md): A phone bill that grows by the same amount per gigabyte plots as a straight line. Similar triangles explain why, and give slope and y = mx + b their meaning.
- [Solving two equations at once: where lines meet](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/algebra/systems-of-equations/index.md): Ten heads and 28 legs: how many chickens and rabbits? Each clue is a line of possibilities, and elimination pivots a line about the point where they cross.
- [Why x⁰ = 1, and negative and fractional exponents](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/algebra/exponents/index.md): Powers of 2 halve as the exponent drops, and one rule, add exponents when you multiply, forces 2⁰ = 1, 2⁻¹ = 1/2 and 2^(1/2) = √2.
- [Absolute value is distance: solving |x − a| < r](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/algebra/inequalities-absolute-value/index.md): Read |x − 3| < 2 as "x is within 2 of 3" and the answer, 1 < x < 5, can be seen on a number line. Also why multiplying by a negative flips an inequality.

## Geometry

Visual geometry lessons with animated proofs: angle sums, the Pythagorean theorem, the area of a circle, similar triangles, inscribed angles and the volume of cones and spheres.

- [Why the angles of a triangle add to 180°](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/geometry/triangle-angle-sum/index.md): Tear the corners off any triangle and they line up along a straight edge. A single parallel line explains why, and a sphere shows the line is needed.
- [The Pythagorean theorem: a proof you can see](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/geometry/pythagorean-theorem/index.md): Why the squares on the two short sides of a right triangle add up to the square on the long side, proved by moving four triangles inside a box.
- [Why the area of a circle is πr²](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/geometry/area-of-a-circle/index.md): The number π is defined by the distance around a circle. Cutting the circle into sectors, and then into rings, shows why the same π gives its area.
- [Similar triangles and why area grows as the square](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/geometry/similar-triangles/index.md): Scaling multiplies every length by one factor and keeps every angle. That explains shadows, maps, and why a pizza twice as wide is four times the pizza.
- [The inscribed angle theorem and Thales' semicircle](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/geometry/inscribed-angle/index.md): From every point on one arc of a circle, a chord is seen under the same angle, half the angle at the center. Two isosceles triangles explain why.
- [Why a cone is a third of a cylinder, and a sphere's volume](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/geometry/volume-of-cone-and-sphere/index.md): A cone holds exactly one third of the cylinder around it. A cube cut into three pyramids shows why, and the same slicing idea gives the volume of a sphere.

## Trigonometry

Visual trigonometry lessons: the unit circle, radians, the Pythagorean identity, angle addition formulas, the laws of sines and cosines, and sine waves.

- [The unit circle: sine and cosine as coordinates](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/trigonometry/unit-circle/index.md): Sine and cosine start as ratios in a right triangle, which stops at 90°. Placing the triangle in a circle of radius 1 extends them to every angle.
- [Radians: measuring an angle by the arc it cuts](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/trigonometry/radians/index.md): A radian is the angle whose arc is as long as the radius. With it, arc length, sector area and the rule sin θ ≈ θ need no conversion constants.
- [Pythagorean identity: why sin² + cos² = 1](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/trigonometry/pythagorean-identity/index.md): The identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 is the Pythagorean theorem on the unit circle. Tangent and secant are lengths in the same picture and give two more.
- [Angle addition formulas: sin(a + b) from one picture](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/trigonometry/angle-addition/index.md): The sine of a sum is not the sum of the sines. Two stacked right triangles show what it is, and a rotated chord proves the formulas for every angle.
- [Law of cosines and law of sines: solving any triangle](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/trigonometry/law-of-sines-and-cosines/index.md): The law of cosines is the Pythagorean theorem corrected for angles other than 90°. With the law of sines it solves any triangle, two-answer case included.
- [Sine waves: amplitude, frequency and phase](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/trigonometry/sine-waves/index.md): A sine wave is the height of a point on a turning wheel. Amplitude, frequency and phase change the wheel, and explain how two waves add, cancel or beat.

## Precalculus

Visual precalculus lessons: function transformations, exponential growth and e, logarithms, complex numbers as rotations, Euler's formula and geometric series.

- [Shifting and stretching graphs: why f(x - 2) moves right](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/precalculus/functions-and-transformations/index.md): Adding 2 outside a function lifts its graph, but subtracting 2 inside moves it right. A graph is a set of points, and tracking one point explains why.
- [Compound interest and where e comes from](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/precalculus/exponential-growth-and-e/index.md): Pay 100% interest in more and more instalments and a dollar grows to 2, 2.25, 2.44, 2.61, and then stops short of 2.72. That ceiling is the number e.
- [What a logarithm is: turning multiplication into addition](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/precalculus/logarithms/index.md): A logarithm answers "what exponent gives this number?". Because exponents add when powers multiply, logarithms turn every product into a sum.
- [Complex numbers: why multiplying by i is a quarter turn](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/precalculus/complex-numbers/index.md): No number on the line squares to -1. Read multiplication by -1 as a half turn and the missing number appears: a quarter turn, which needs a second axis.
- [Euler's formula: why e^(iπ) = -1](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/precalculus/eulers-formula/index.md): You cannot multiply e by itself iπ times, so the famous equation needs a definition first. Compound interest supplies one, and it leads around a circle.
- [Geometric series, and why 0.999... equals 1](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/precalculus/geometric-series/index.md): What it means to add infinitely many numbers, when a geometric series has a sum, the formula a/(1 - r) with proof, and why 0.999... is exactly 1.
- [Roots, factors and the shape of a polynomial](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/precalculus/polynomials-and-roots/index.md): A cubic crosses the x axis once or three times, never exactly twice. The factor theorem, multiplicity and the leading term explain why, with proofs.

## Calculus

Visual calculus lessons: what a derivative is, the power, product and chain rules, limits, integrals, the fundamental theorem of calculus and Taylor series, with animations of every idea.

- [What is a derivative? Speed at a single instant](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/calculus/what-is-a-derivative/index.md): A falling ball has a speed at every instant, but an instant is too short to measure a speed over. The derivative is the precise idea that resolves this.
- [Why the derivative of x² is 2x: the power rule from pictures](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/calculus/power-rule/index.md): A growing square gains two thin strips and a tiny corner. That picture explains the 2 in 2x, and counting the same pieces in general proves the power rule.
- [The product rule and the chain rule, seen](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/calculus/product-and-chain-rule/index.md): A rectangle whose sides both change explains the product rule, and a nudge passed along a chain of number lines explains the chain rule. Both are then proved.
- [Why the derivative of sine is cosine](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/calculus/derivative-of-sine/index.md): Nudge a point around the unit circle and a tiny triangle appears, similar to the big one. Its legs are the derivatives of sine and cosine.
- [What is a limit? The epsilon-delta definition, explained](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/calculus/limits/index.md): A limit is a game. You name a tolerance, I answer with a window. From that one definition we prove the limit laws and the squeeze theorem.
- [What is an integral? Adding up to get area](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/calculus/integrals/index.md): Distance from a changing speed, found by slicing time into pieces and adding. The definite integral is the limit of those sums, defined precisely and computed.
- [The fundamental theorem of calculus, explained and proved](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/calculus/fundamental-theorem/index.md): Why area and slope undo each other. The rate at which an area grows is the height of the curve, and that turns every integral into a subtraction.
- [Taylor series: building functions out of polynomials](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/calculus/taylor-series/index.md): How a calculator finds cos(0.3) with only addition and multiplication, why factorials appear, how large the error can be, and where the method breaks.
- [Maxima and minima: where the slope is zero](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/calculus/optimization/index.md): To fence the largest field or make the cheapest can, look where the derivative is zero, and also at the ends. Why that works, and when it does not.

## Linear Algebra

Visual linear algebra lessons: vectors, matrices as linear transformations, matrix multiplication, determinants, dot products and eigenvectors, shown as animations of the plane.

- [What is a vector? Arrows, lists of numbers, and adding them](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/linear-algebra/vectors/index.md): A vector is a list of numbers read as a movement. Adding entry by entry matches placing arrows tip to tail, and two non-parallel arrows reach the whole plane.
- [A matrix is a transformation of space](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/linear-algebra/matrices-as-transformations/index.md): A 2x2 matrix moves every point of the plane, and its two columns say where the basis arrows land. Linearity is why those four numbers settle everything else.
- [Why matrix multiplication is defined the way it is](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/linear-algebra/matrix-multiplication/index.md): Multiplying matrices means doing one transformation after another. The rows-times-columns rule, the failure of AB = BA and associativity all follow from that.
- [The determinant is how much area gets scaled](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/linear-algebra/determinant/index.md): A matrix multiplies every area in the plane by one number, ad - bc. That explains its sign, why det(AB) = det(A)det(B), and which matrices can be undone.
- [The dot product: projection, angle and why the formula works](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/linear-algebra/dot-product/index.md): Multiply matching coordinates and add. The result measures how far one arrow reaches along another, which gives angles, projections and Cauchy-Schwarz.
- [Eigenvectors: the directions a transformation leaves alone](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/linear-algebra/eigenvectors/index.md): Most arrows are knocked off their line by a matrix. The few that are only stretched are its eigenvectors, and they turn matrix powers into powers of numbers.
- [Solving Ax = b by undoing a transformation](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/linear-algebra/linear-systems-and-inverses/index.md): A linear system asks which vector a matrix sends to b. That view explains when there is one solution, none or a whole line, and what the inverse matrix does.

## Multivariable Calculus

Visual multivariable calculus lessons: contour maps, partial derivatives, the gradient, Lagrange multipliers, double integrals, divergence, curl and Green's theorem.

- [Surfaces and contour maps: functions of two variables](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/multivariable-calculus/functions-of-two-variables/index.md): A hiking map shows a mountain on flat paper. Its contour lines are the level sets of a function of two variables, and their spacing measures steepness.
- [The gradient: which way is uphill?](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/multivariable-calculus/partial-derivatives-and-gradient/index.md): On a hillside the slope depends on the direction you face. Partial derivatives give two of those slopes, and the gradient packs all of them into one arrow.
- [Lagrange multipliers: the best point on a path](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/multivariable-calculus/lagrange-multipliers/index.md): The highest point of a trail is where the trail just touches a contour line. There the gradients of the height and of the constraint are parallel.
- [Double integrals: volume under a surface](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/multivariable-calculus/double-integrals/index.md): Volume under a surface is a limit of sums of thin columns. Slicing turns it into two ordinary integrals, and polar coordinates handle round regions.
- [Divergence and curl: reading a vector field](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/multivariable-calculus/divergence-and-curl/index.md): Two numbers at each point of a flow. Divergence is the net outflow from a tiny square per unit area, and curl is the circulation around it per unit area.
- [Green's theorem: the inside read from the boundary](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/multivariable-calculus/greens-theorem/index.md): A walk around the edge of a region, adding up a vector field along the way, equals the integral of the field's curl over the inside. Here is why.

## Probability

Visual probability lessons: sample spaces, conditional probability, Bayes' rule, the birthday paradox, expected value, the binomial distribution and the law of large numbers.

- [What probability means: counting equally likely outcomes](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/probability/sample-spaces/index.md): Is a total of 7 with two dice three times as likely as a 12, or six times? Settling it leads to sample spaces, events and the rules every probability obeys.
- [Bayes' rule: why a positive test is usually a false alarm](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/probability/conditional-probability-bayes/index.md): A 99% accurate test for a rare disease comes back positive, and the chance you are sick is about 9%. Conditional probability and Bayes' theorem explain why.
- [The birthday paradox: why 23 people is enough](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/probability/birthday-paradox/index.md): In a room of 23 people, two probably share a birthday. The exact formula, why the answer grows like a square root, and what the model assumes.
- [Expected value and the surprising power of adding averages](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/probability/expected-value/index.md): The expected value of a random quantity is its long-run average. Expected values add even for dependent quantities, which solves the hat-check problem.
- [Binomial distribution: Pascal's triangle and a Galton board](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/probability/binomial-distribution/index.md): Balls bouncing through rows of pegs pile up in the middle. Counting their paths gives Pascal's triangle and the binomial formula, with its mean and variance.
- [The law of large numbers, and the gambler's fallacy](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/probability/law-of-large-numbers/index.md): A fair coin has no memory, yet its share of heads settles at one half. The weak law of large numbers says exactly how, and Chebyshev's inequality proves it.
- [Monty Hall problem: why switching wins two times in three](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/probability/monty-hall/index.md): Three doors, one car, and a host who opens a goat door. Switching wins 2/3 of the time. Three solutions, and why the answer depends on what the host knows.

## Statistics

Visual statistics lessons: mean and standard deviation, the normal distribution, the central limit theorem, standard error, confidence intervals, p-values and regression.

- [Mean, median and standard deviation: what each one says](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/statistics/mean-median-spread/index.md): The mean is a balance point, the median is a middle, and the standard deviation is a typical distance. Each is the best answer to a precise question.
- [The normal distribution and the 68-95-99.7 rule](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/statistics/normal-distribution/index.md): A histogram with ever narrower bins settles onto a curve whose areas are probabilities. For the bell curve, those areas give the 68-95-99.7 rule and z-scores.
- [The central limit theorem: why bell curves are everywhere](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/statistics/central-limit-theorem/index.md): One die is flat, but the average of 30 dice follows a bell curve. The central limit theorem says when this happens, how fast, and when it fails.
- [Standard error: how 1,000 people speak for a country](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/statistics/sampling-and-standard-error/index.md): A random sample's accuracy depends on its own size, not on the population's. We prove the square-root law for the standard error and see its limits.
- [What a 95% confidence interval does and does not say](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/statistics/confidence-intervals/index.md): We derive the interval mean ± 1.96 standard errors, test its 95% coverage by simulation, and go through the common misreadings and why each is wrong.
- [P-values and hypothesis tests without the mysticism](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/statistics/p-values/index.md): A coin lands heads 60 times in 100. We compute the exact p-value, define the two kinds of error, and show with Bayes' theorem what a p-value is not.
- [Correlation and the line of best fit, derived](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/statistics/correlation-and-regression/index.md): We derive the least-squares line, define the correlation r and prove it lies between -1 and 1, then explain regression to the mean and why r is not causation.

## Discrete Mathematics

Visual discrete mathematics lessons: permutations and combinations, Pascal's triangle, the pigeonhole principle, induction, graph theory, modular arithmetic and the probabilistic method.

- [Permutations and combinations: counting without listing](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/discrete-math/permutations-and-combinations/index.md): Five runners and three medals give 60 podiums but only 10 groups of medalists. The product rule, permutations and combinations, each one proved.
- [Pascal's triangle and the binomial theorem](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/discrete-math/pascals-triangle/index.md): Routes across a street grid and the coefficients of (a + b)^n are the same numbers. We prove Pascal's rule, the binomial theorem and the row sums by counting.
- [The pigeonhole principle: obvious, and surprisingly strong](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/discrete-math/pigeonhole-principle/index.md): More objects than boxes forces two into one box. We prove the principle and its general form, then use it on problems where finding the boxes is the hard part.
- [Mathematical induction: infinitely many dominoes](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/discrete-math/induction/index.md): How a finite argument proves infinitely many statements. Induction stated exactly, used on a sum and a tiling, and a famous false proof taken apart.
- [Bridges of Königsberg: Euler paths and circuits](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/discrete-math/graphs-euler-paths/index.md): Seven bridges and a walk that nobody could find. Counting the edges at each vertex proves it cannot exist and settles every draw-without-lifting puzzle.
- [Fibonacci numbers and thinking recursively](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/discrete-math/fibonacci-and-recursion/index.md): Count the ways to climb a staircase and the Fibonacci numbers appear. Their rule, two identities, Binet's formula and the golden ratio, all proved.
- [Clock arithmetic: modular arithmetic and why it works](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/discrete-math/modular-arithmetic/index.md): Arithmetic with remainders, made exact. Congruences, the divisibility tests for 9 and 11, when division is allowed, and Fermat's little theorem, with proofs.
- [The probabilistic method: Ramsey numbers by coin flips](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/discrete-math/the-probabilistic-method/index.md): Six party guests always include three mutual friends or three mutual strangers. For larger parties, the best lower bounds come from coloring at random.

## Logic and Proof

Visual lessons in logic and proof: truth tables, implication and the contrapositive, quantifiers, proof by contradiction, sets and Cantor's diagonal argument.

- [Truth tables: and, or, not as calculation](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/logic/truth-tables/index.md): The word "or" has two meanings in English. Truth tables fix one, and turn questions about what sentences mean into finite calculations you can check row by row.
- [If-then statements: converse and contrapositive](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/logic/implication/index.md): When is "if P then Q" true? One table answers it, shows why the contrapositive says the same thing and the converse does not, and solves the four-card puzzle.
- [Quantifiers: for all, there exists, and negation](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/logic/quantifiers/index.md): Everyone loves someone" has two meanings. Quantifiers separate them, show how to negate each, and turn the epsilon-delta definition of a limit into a game.
- [Proof by contradiction: why √2 is not a fraction](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/logic/proof-by-contradiction/index.md): No fraction squares to exactly 2. To prove it, assume one does and follow the assumption until it breaks. That method is proof by contradiction.
- [Sets, Venn diagrams and inclusion-exclusion](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/logic/sets-and-counting/index.md): Union, intersection and complement defined exactly, De Morgan's laws for sets, and how to count a union of overlapping sets without counting anything twice.
- [Cantor's diagonal argument: some infinities are bigger](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/logic/infinity-cantor/index.md): Sizes of infinite sets are compared by pairing. The integers and the fractions pair off with the counting numbers, and the real numbers provably do not.

## Physics

Visual physics lessons: velocity and acceleration, Newton's second law, projectile motion, conservation of energy, momentum, simple harmonic motion and waves.

- [Position, velocity and acceleration: reading motion graphs](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/physics/motion-graphs/index.md): Slope turns a position graph into velocity and velocity into acceleration; area goes back. The constant-acceleration equations come from one trapezoid.
- [Newton's second law, F = ma: what force really does](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/physics/newtons-second-law/index.md): Forces change an object's velocity; none is needed to keep it moving. Newton's three laws, free-body diagrams, the incline and the Atwood machine in full.
- [Projectile motion: dropped and fired bullets land together](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/physics/projectile-motion/index.md): Gravity acts only on the vertical part of a projectile's motion. From that come the parabola, the time of flight, the range, and why 45 degrees goes farthest.
- [Conservation of energy: a roller coaster's bookkeeping](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/physics/energy-conservation/index.md): Work, kinetic and potential energy, and the work-energy theorem, derived from F = ma and used to find a coaster's speed anywhere and the height a loop needs.
- [Momentum and collisions: what survives a crash](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/physics/momentum-collisions/index.md): Momentum, impulse and Newton's third law, and how they fix the outcome of sticky and bouncy collisions when energy alone gives the wrong answer.
- [Simple harmonic motion: springs and pendulums](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/physics/simple-harmonic-motion/index.md): Why a mass on a spring takes the same time per swing however far it is pulled: Hooke's law and the shadow of circular motion, and why a pendulum nearly does.
- [Waves and interference: how two ripples can cancel](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/physics/waves-and-interference/index.md): What a wave is, why its speed is frequency times wavelength, and how adding waves gives the quiet lines of an interference pattern and the notes of a string.
- [Circular motion, gravity and why the Moon doesn't fall](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/physics/circular-motion-and-orbits/index.md): The acceleration v²/r of circular motion, derived from the velocity triangle, and what it says about satellites, Kepler's third law and weightlessness.

## Economics

Visual economics lessons: supply and demand, elasticity, marginal cost and revenue, consumer surplus and taxes, compound interest, comparative advantage and game theory.

- [Supply and demand: where a price comes from](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/economics/supply-and-demand/index.md): Line up buyers by what they would pay and sellers by what they would accept. The price where the two counts match is the one that leaves nobody turned away.
- [Elasticity: when raising the price lowers revenue](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/economics/elasticity/index.md): Revenue is a rectangle under the demand curve. Elasticity compares percentage changes in quantity and price, and decides whether a price rise grows it.
- [Thinking at the margin: marginal cost and revenue](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/economics/marginal-thinking/index.md): The right question is what one more unit adds to revenue and to cost. Why averages mislead, why sunk costs drop out, and why profit peaks where MR meets MC.
- [Consumer surplus, and what a tax destroys](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/economics/surplus-and-taxes/index.md): Measure what a market is worth to its buyers and sellers, then tax it. Some of the loss reaches nobody, and who bears the rest depends on slopes, not the law.
- [Compound interest and the time value of money](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/economics/compound-interest-present-value/index.md): Why a dollar today is worth more than a dollar later, how to price future payments, and where the rule of 72 and the mortgage formula come from.
- [Comparative advantage: why trade helps both sides](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/economics/comparative-advantage/index.md): Someone who is better at everything still gains by trading with someone who is worse at everything. Opportunity cost explains why, and a short proof shows when.
- [The prisoner's dilemma and Nash equilibrium](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/economics/game-theory/index.md): How to read a payoff table, find best responses and Nash equilibria, mix strategies when no cell is stable, and see why repeated play can sustain cooperation.

## Machine Learning

Visual machine learning lessons: least squares, gradient descent, logistic regression, neurons and neural networks, backpropagation and overfitting.

- [What "learning" means: fitting a line to data](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/machine-learning/fitting-a-line/index.md): A model is a formula with adjustable numbers, a loss scores its misses, and training lowers the loss. All three, worked by hand on four house prices.
- [Gradient descent: learning by walking downhill](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/machine-learning/gradient-descent/index.md): Derive the gradient descent update from the tangent line, prove exactly which learning rates converge on a parabola, and watch it train a line on real data.
- [Classification: drawing a line between yes and no](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/machine-learning/logistic-regression/index.md): Logistic regression from the ground up: the sigmoid from log-odds, cross-entropy from maximum likelihood, the gradient derived in full, and why XOR defeats it.
- [What a neural network computes](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/machine-learning/neural-networks/index.md): A neuron is a linear score followed by a bend. Sums of bends build bumps, bumps build any curve, and two neurons solve XOR. All with explicit weights.
- [Backpropagation: the chain rule, organized](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/machine-learning/backpropagation/index.md): Run a tiny network forward with real numbers, get every weight's slope in one backward pass, prove the delta recursion, and check it by nudging each weight.
- [Overfitting: when a model memorizes instead of learning](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/machine-learning/overfitting/index.md): Fit polynomials of degree 1, 3 and 9 to ten noisy points, watch training and test error part ways, and derive the bias-variance decomposition.
- [k-means: finding groups nobody labeled](https://www.monocurl.com/monocurl-essays/machine-learning/k-means-clustering/index.md): Score a grouping by its sum of squared distances, lower it with Lloyd's two alternating steps, prove the algorithm must stop, and see where it goes wrong.
